blogs.title: The Consistency Ratchet: How DuPont Factor Six Was Corrected by Factor Two
blogs.description: In a complex patchwork of trademark law principles, Apex Bank v. CC Serve Corp. clarifies the strict relationship between DuPont Factors Two and Six. We examine the Federal Circuit's decision that when a Board determines services are 'highly similar' under the second DuPont factor, the Board cannot arbitrarily narrow the scope of marks it reviews under the sixth. This post analyzes the 'consistency ratchet' that requires a rigorous alignment of priority when assessing third-party similar marks across the multi-factor confusion test.

blogs.title: Legal Identification of Financial Services: When 'Banking' and 'Credit Cards' Become One Mark
blogs.description: A fundamental tension exists in financial sector litigation regarding whether distinct service descriptions constitute separate trademarks. The Federal Circuit affirmed that 'credit card services' and 'banking and financing services' may be 'legally identical' for the purposes of likelihood of confusion. Here, we dissect the Board's definition of related goods and how an appellate court scrutinized whether a 'partnered bank' and 'credit card issuer' were sufficiently divergent to avoid confusion under the Lanham Act.

blogs.title: The Domino Effect of Vacatur: When a Single DuPont Error Cascades Across Factors
blogs.description: Trademark appeals often suffer from piecemeal analysis, but Apex Bank forces a new disciplined review of interconnected factors. We analyze why the Federal Circuit vacated the Board's analysis on DuPont Factor Six—and subsequently Factor One—due to the technical error regarding commodity scope. This post explores the procedural implications of this 'cascade remand,' offering insight on how courts ensure that a flaw in one factor's methodology does not invalidate a factor's independent analysis.
